conviction_note: Findings sum to +2.7, mostly positioning (about 25% of shares short at 13 days to cover, call-side skew of -14 vol points) and a low EPS bar, against a seasonal Q3 that consensus only partly reflects. The scaled number is far smaller (p_up 52 x abs 13 = +0.52) because this name has sold its last revenue beat (Q2 2026: revenue beat, EPS miss, -5.3%). The new CFO's first call and the promised outlook revisit, with PAD Aviation margin dilution not yet quantified, make the guide line a genuine coin flip. The gap between the two numbers is that reaction-function uncertainty, not inconsistency.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $181.8M and EPS $0.27 (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-10-28, https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/TMDX/22402; Zacks revenue consensus $181.8M, +26.4% y/y, https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:f148dc073094b:0-reasons-to-retain-transmedics-stock-in-your-portfolio-for-now/). Futu preview of 2026-10-31 has revenue at about $178.05M (https://www.futunn.com/en/stock/TMDX-US/news), so the revenue bar sits in a $178-182M band from agreeing sources. The EPS bar has one current source: an older iTiger preview carried $0.46, but it predates Q2. EPS findings are therefore capped small. Company FY26 guide is $737-757M ex-PAD Aviation (8-K 2026-08-04 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001756262/000119312526332767/tmdx-ex99_1.htm), reiterated 2026-09-10 with a promise to revisit at Q3. FY26 adjusted operating margin guide was cut to about 12.5-14% from about 16% (Q2 call). Guide math: H1 was $363.9M, so H2 is $373-393M; at the $181.8M Q3 bar, Q4 is implied at $191-211M.
positioning_check: Short interest: about 8.6M shares short at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, 13.1 days to cover (8.0M / 10.7 days at 09-15). Snippet only: curvedtrading.com/stocks/tmdx/short-interest returned 403 on fetch. With about 34.6M shares outstanding (AAII 2026-11-05) that is about 25% of shares. Earlier, 7.36M / 5.32 days at 2026-05-29 (equibles). Short interest has been building into the print. Skew_25d is -14.31 vol points: calls bid over puts, 'upside paid'. Put/call OI is 0.72. The 1-day straddle is 17.04%, but the ATM spread is 38% of mid, so that figure is indicative only. Counter-flow: a $187K bearish risk reversal on 2026-10-30 (Futu headline). Earnings Whispers puts bearish sentiment at about 13%, down from 42% before the last report. The stock is -54.5% from its 52-week high and -13.5% over 20 days, and was down about 6% intraday on the print day with no news found (AAII 2026-11-05).

findings.finding: The Q3 seasonal decline the consensus bakes in looks too shallow. Consensus at $181.8M implies -4.3% q/q from Q2's record $189.9M. In Q3 2025 revenue fell -8.6% q/q ($157.4M to $143.8M), and in Q3 2024 it fell about -4.8%. On the Aug 4 call management warned that August vacations would slow centres and that Q3 'may not match Q2's strength'. Repeating 2025's seasonal step gives about $173.6M, a ~4.5% miss. Partial offsets: July 2026 was the highest aviation month in company history (CEO, same call), and the logistics account won from a competitor in Q2 carries into Q3. Net expectation: about a 1% revenue shortfall against the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: revenue $143.8M against roughly $145M consensus, a slight miss; stock +1.09% (baseline). Q2 2026: revenue $189.9M beat $184.2M but EPS missed; stock -5.28%. Q1 2026 (May): -23.19%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus has already come down, from about $184M before Q2 to $178-182M. A fully priced last-year seasonal pattern would put the bar near $174M, not $181.8M. Earnings Whispers itself calls the implied Q4 ramp 'steep', which says the Street has not fully marked Q3 down to seasonality.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 and Q2/Q3 2025 revenue come from company 8-Ks (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001756262/000119312526332767/tmdx-ex99_1.htm). The bar comes from Earnings Whispers (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/TMDX/22402). The seasonality warning and the July record come from the same call summary, so they count once here. No 2026 Q3 flight-tracker or OPTN figure was found to settle it.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-10, about 70 days into Q3 with July and August in hand, management reiterated FY26 revenue of $737-757M in an 8-K (CFO-change release) and said it would 'revisit this outlook in conjunction with its third quarter 2026 results'. A company tracking toward the low end would not usually reaffirm mid-quarter. Director David Weill bought 1,336 shares at $81.63 the next day (Form 4).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: low end of the guide raised to $737M, stock -5.3% anyway, on margin. Q1 2026: guide reiterated, stock -23%. This name has not paid for revenue-guide holds; the margin guide is what has moved it.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock fell after the reiteration (Quiverquant headline: 'slides after CFO transition news despite reaffirmed 2026 outlook') and is down about 16% from $81.63 since. The market has read the CFO change as the news and discounted the mid-quarter reaffirmation. If the reaffirmation were priced, the stock would not be at $68 with a revenue bar sitting inside the guide.
findings.independence: Director open-market purchase on 2026-09-11, Form 4: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001756262/000119312526390650/ownership.xml (small, about $109k). It shares a date with the 8-K, not a document.

findings.finding: This is a new CFO's first print, and the outlook revisit is pre-announced. Fernando Araujo (ex GE HealthCare) started 2026-09-21, replacing Gerardo Hernandez. The 8-K says the outlook will be revisited at Q3, and on the Q2 call management said PAD Aviation consolidation starting in Q3 'will be dilutive to both gross margin and operating margin' but could not quantify it until Q3. The H2 gross-margin guide is already about 59%. This sets up a margin reset (PAD dilution plus kidney spend) on the line this stock has sold off on twice in 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: adjusted operating-margin guide cut from about 16% to 12.5-14%, stock -5.3% despite a revenue beat. Q1 2026: EPS/margin miss, stock -23%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: EPS consensus has been cut to $0.27 against $0.44 actual in Q2, and Earnings Whispers says investors are 'braced for weak profits'. What is not priced is the size of PAD's dilution, which no one outside the company has (deal terms undisclosed). A priced margin reset would show up as put skew, and the skew is call-side.
findings.independence: Same 8-K as the reiteration finding (one document read two ways: revenue reaffirmed vs. outlook-revisit risk). The PAD margin warning is from the Q2 call summary (https://vectorshift.ai/research/companies/transmedics-group/earnings/2026-q2). PAD deal terms are undisclosed (https://investors.transmedics.com/news-releases/news-release-details/transmedics-group-announces-completion-strategic-investment-pad).

findings.finding: The EPS bar is low. Consensus Q3 EPS is $0.27 against $0.44 adjusted in Q2 2026 and $0.66 in Q3 2025, a 39% sequential drop. H2 opex was guided 'broadly in line with H1', with R&D elevated and SG&A tightly managed. Revenue near the bar with flat opex would land above $0.27 unless PAD dilution is large. The EPS bar has only one current source, so this is capped small.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 EPS beat by about 33% and the stock fell about 2% then -4.3% (baseline 2026-02-24). Q2 2026 EPS missed $0.50 at $0.44, stock -5.3%. EPS misses have been punished; beats have not been paid.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar was cut hard after Q2. If the street expected a beat, the whisper would sit above $0.27 and sentiment would not be described as braced for weak profits.
findings.independence: Q2 adjusted EPS of $0.44 and the H2 opex commentary come from the company 8-K / call (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001756262/000119312526332767/tmdx-ex99_1.htm). The older iTiger preview carried $0.46 (https://www.itiger.com/news/1138296569), so the EPS bar is disputed.

findings.finding: Positioning: short interest rose to about 8.6M shares (about 25% of 34.6M shares out) with 13.1 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement, up from 7.36M / 5.3 days in May. The options market pays up for calls (25-delta skew -14.3 vol points), and the stock is -54.5% from its high and -13.5% over 20 days. Any print that is not a clear miss has a squeeze mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-05-08 print +19.64% and 2025-07-30 +10.46%: squeezes on a heavily shorted name when volume beat. Short interest also did not stop -23% in May 2026, when margin disappointed.
findings.why_not_priced: The call-side skew suggests the options market has partly priced squeeze risk. What is not priced is how short the float is going into a quarter with a low EPS bar: 13 days to cover means covering cannot happen in one session.
findings.independence: Baseline skew -14.31 and 'upside paid' (sealed baseline). Earlier short-interest record: equibles 2026-05-29 (https://equibles.com/stocks/tmdx/short-interest). Counter-signal: a $187K bearish risk reversal on 2026-10-30 (Futu, https://www.futunn.com/en/stock/TMDX-US/news).

findings.finding: On 2026-10-30 CMS issued the final OPO Conditions for Coverage rule (CMS-3409-F) and stated it 'will be moving to decertify tier 3 OPOs as indicated in the 2020 final rule'. Tier 2 status alone is no longer grounds for decertification. Management called the OPO decision 'binary', excluded OPO upside from guidance, and has argued that reform raises organ supply. The rule settles the regulatory path and gives the call a positive talking point for 2027 volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured on this line; the OPO reform has been a narrative item, not a print driver.
findings.why_not_priced: It came out six days before the print in a regulatory fact sheet that does not name the company, and no analyst note tying it to TMDX was found. It is a macro-to-company transmission the company has not yet confirmed.
findings.independence: Q2 call: OPO upside excluded from guidance, decision 'binary' (https://vectorshift.ai/research/companies/transmedics-group/earnings/2026-q2). This is a proxy, sized small.

findings.finding: Sell-side tracking shops leaned positive into the print. TD Cowen, which publishes TMDX flight and transplant tracking, reiterated Buy with a $120 target on 2026-11-02. Piper Sandler reiterated Buy with a $100 target on 2026-11-03. Barclays initiated at Buy, $120, on 2026-10-06. Canaccord trimmed its target to $94 on 2026-10-13 (a snippet says it raised Q3 estimates). Against that, Stifel kept Hold at $65 on 2026-10-15, and AAII counts 2 downgrades and 0 upgrades in the month to 2026-11-04.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: TD Cowen's flight-data reiterations ahead of Q2 2026 (July 1) preceded a revenue beat that the stock sold (-5.3%).
findings.why_not_priced: The note text is not public, so the flight-tracking content behind the reiterations is unseen. If the trackers showed a Q3 miss, a pre-print downgrade or estimate cut from the tracking shops would be expected, and none was found.
findings.independence: Futu headline list (Barclays initiation, Canaccord target cut): https://www.futunn.com/en/stock/TMDX-US/news. AAII downgrade count: https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/554060-why-transmedics-group-inc8217s-tmdx-stock-is-down-608. This is a proxy with no flight numbers.

findings.finding: PAD Aviation (a German charter operator with nine Phenom 300s and more than 40 pilots; terms undisclosed) is consolidated from Q3. Reported Q3 revenue therefore includes non-guided PAD revenue while the guide excludes it, so headline revenue may clear the $181.8M bar mechanically even if the organic business is soft, with margins diluted.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has sold low-quality revenue beats (Q2 2026: revenue beat, margin down, -5.3%).
findings.why_not_priced: Whether the $178-182M consensus includes PAD is not stated in any preview found. PAD's revenue has never been disclosed, so no estimate can embed it with confidence.
findings.independence: Q2 call: consolidation from Q3, dilutive, unquantified (https://vectorshift.ai/research/companies/transmedics-group/earnings/2026-q2). It shares the PAD fact with the CFO/margin finding, but the lines differ (revenue headline here, margin there).

outside_window.finding: XVIVO filed its PMA for the XVIVO Heart Assist Transport System (FDA receipt 2026-09-28, PRESERVE IDE with 141 patients at 14 US centres). An approval would bring the first US commercial competitor to OCS Heart (about $33M of Q2 revenue). The decision is dated well after the window.
CHOPS IDE-supplement approval was expected late Q3 or early Q4 2026 (Q2 call); the 510(k) is targeted for H1 2027. No approval announcement was found, and the 510(k) resolves after the window.

baseline_tension: The evidence mostly agrees with the call-side skew and the crowded short (mild upside lean). The one fundamental negative, Q3 seasonality, cuts against it but sits inside what management already warned of. The 20-day drawdown and today's ~6% slide have lowered the bar, so the net lean is barely positive and p_up stays at 52.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar): the EPS bar has one current source ($0.27; an older $0.46 conflicts), so the low-EPS-bar finding was capped from +1.0 to +0.5. The revenue bar ($178-182M) has two agreeing sources and stands.
Rule 6 / core table (inside the guide): the Q3 seasonality miss lands inside what management warned on the Aug 4 call, so -1.0 was moved toward 0.
Rule 7 (crowded short, call skew): both negatives shrunk. Seasonality went to -0.6 in total (with the rule-6 move, one cut per concern) and the CFO/margin reset from -1.0 to -0.7.
Rule 1 (reaction function): already reflected. p_up stays at 52 because this name sold its Q2 revenue beat; no second cut to findings.
Rule 5 (proxy): the analyst reiterations and CMS OPO rule were already small and stay as filed proxies; nothing else changed.
